role: cross-tissue directional concordance / metadata-audit stress test
NOT: independent replication, validation, or confirmatory evidence
declared_design: This study compared the genome-wide expression in human trabecular meshwork tissue between 13 controls and 15 POAG cases. Six controls and one POAG cases had the expression performed from both left and right eyes. One technical replicate was done between two cases. The average from the biological replicates for each inidividual was used for analysis.
series_summary: This study compared genome-wide expression profiles of individuals with and without Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma (POAG). One POAG case (case #6 with two replicates #10 and #11) carried a Q368X myocilin mutation.

confounding.covariates: no ancestry/age/sex; M2 reduces to [1, glaucoma]

poag_correlation_merges.support: highest POAG pair; consistent with GEO 'case #6 with two replicates'

array_level.description: All 36 deposited arrays treated as independent (the naive reuse).

donor_metadata.description: Controls collapsed by postmortem delay (13 donors); POAG arrays left separate because deposited metadata cannot pair them. Known residual pseudo-replication on the case side.

donor_declared.description: As donor_metadata plus two disjoint highest-correlation POAG pairs merged by averaging, reproducing the declared 15 cases / 13 controls. The second merge is an unverifiable, data-driven assumption.

interpretation: Directional concordance is descriptive only (n=6 transcripts; no inference, no p-value). Disease is perfectly confounded with tissue procurement and postmortem delay, so any case-control contrast in this series is not interpretable as a disease effect. The six-gene result must not be used to support or refute the primary 0/18 finding.
